title: ～わけだ — “so that’s why ～ / no wonder ～”
summary: Used to draw a natural conclusion from facts or a reason: “so that is why ～.” It attaches to the plain form of a verb or adjective (な-adj + な, noun + という). Often paired with 道理で (no wonder) or それで.

patterns.gloss: plain form + わけだ (that’s why / so it is)

patterns.form: 道理で／なるほど＋〜わけだ

body.p: When you learn a fact and a puzzling result suddenly makes sense, you say it with わけだ. 窓が開いている。道理で寒いわけだ。 The listener already knows (or the speaker has just realized) the cause.
It can also restate something logically: 円が安くなった。外国からの客が増えたわけだ。 It sums up the result that naturally follows from the reason.

It states a conclusion with understanding, not a new guess. It is closer to “as expected” than ～はずだ, which just says something should be true. Without 道理で / それで, the sentence still works if the cause was already mentioned.

examples.ja: 道理（どうり）で寒（さむ）いわけだ。窓（まど）が開（あ）いている。
examples.romaji: Douri de samui wake da. Mado ga aite iru.
examples.tr: No wonder it’s cold; the window is open.
examples.note: The reason (open window) explains the puzzling cold.

examples.ja: 一晩中（ひとばんじゅう）起（お）きていたのか。眠（ねむ）そうなわけだ。
examples.romaji: Hitobanjuu okite ita no ka. Nemusou na wake da.
examples.tr: You were up all night? No wonder you look sleepy.

examples.ja: 円（えん）が安（やす）くなったから、外国（がいこく）からの客（きゃく）が増（ふ）えたわけだ。
examples.romaji: En ga yasuku natta kara, gaikoku kara no kyaku ga fueta wake da.
examples.tr: The yen got cheaper, so that’s why visitors from abroad increased.

pitfalls: It is not a guess about an unknown fact. Use it only when the reason is known.
Do not confuse it with わけではない / わけがない / わけにはいかない, which have different meanings.
